description: Single-panel property plot (no sub-panels): Rp (Ω·cm²) obtained from EIS fittings of the surface oxide film on low-density steels versus immersion time (h). The y-axis is linear from 0.0 to 1.6×10^5 Ω·cm² with printed ticks at 0.0, 4.0×10^4, 8.0×10^4, 1.2×10^5 and 1.6×10^5; the x-axis runs 0–168 h with ticks every 24 h. Four series are drawn as coloured point markers with vertical error bars joined by dashed guide lines, identified by an upper-right legend: S0 (red stars), S950 (green open circles), S1050 (blue triangles) and S1150 (magenta squares). Points cluster at short times (about 0.5–12 h) and are then spaced at 24, 72, 120 and 168 h; a pale shaded vertical band spans roughly the first 12 h, marking the initial immersion stage. S950 is highest at every plotted time, rising steeply between about 2 and 12 h and then plateauing just below 1.2×10^5 Ω·cm² after 24 h. S1050 plateaus near 8×10^4 Ω·cm². S1150 and S0 lie close together and lowest, both remaining below roughly 5×10^4 Ω·cm² at 168 h. No numeric data labels are printed. The figure demonstrates that the fine-grained state develops a faster-growing, more stable and more protective oxide film.

observations.observation: The figure is a single scatter/line plot of Rp on a linear Ω·cm² axis (0.0 to 1.6×10^5, ticks at 0.0, 4.0×10^4, 8.0×10^4, 1.2×10^5, 1.6×10^5) against immersion time (h) from 0 to 168 with 24 h ticks.

Four datasets are distinguished by marker shape and colour and listed in an upper-right legend: S0 (red stars), S950 (green open circles), S1050 (blue triangles), S1150 (magenta squares); each series has vertical error bars and is joined by a coloured dashed guide line.
A pale shaded vertical band covers approximately the first 12 h of immersion, highlighting the initial stage where all four curves rise steeply.

The S950 (green circle) curve lies above all other series at every plotted time; it rises steeply between roughly 2 and 12 h and then plateaus just below the 1.2×10^5 Ω·cm² gridline from 24 h to 168 h.
The S1050 (blue triangle) curve is the second highest, rising more slowly and plateauing around the 8.0×10^4 Ω·cm² gridline.
The S1150 (magenta square) and S0 (red star) curves are the lowest two and nearly overlap; both stay below roughly 5×10^4 Ω·cm² over the whole 168 h, with S1150 slightly above S0 at long times.
No numeric data labels are printed on the plot; all values must be read against the y-axis gridlines.
The caption states these Rp values come from EIS fittings of the surface oxide film on the LDSs after immersion for different times.

The citing text states the fine-grained sample S950 reaches 114.9 kΩ·cm² at 168 h, significantly higher than the coarse-grained S1150 at 50.6 kΩ·cm²; these numbers are consistent with the plotted plateau heights but are not printed in the figure.
The citing text states the Rp value of S950 increases rapidly during the initial immersion stage (2–8 h) and then stabilizes after approximately 24 h.
The citing text states that coarse-grained samples show lower initial Rp values and slower growth rates with immersion time, indicating delayed oxide-film formation.
The citing text states the variation among parallel samples is within 5 % and that the impedance evolution trend is repeatable.

unreadable_items: Exact magnitudes of the error bars are not readable as numbers (no error values printed)
Printed numeric values for individual data points are absent, so points can only be located relative to gridlines
